note: He told MoneyLIFE (2007) he came back in 1981, and McKinsey's 2025 introduction also says 1981. CNN Editorial Research says he withdrew in 1980. We use his own date in the story and show both in the glance facts.

claim: Whether he holds a Stanford MBA
note: Reliance's chairman page says he 'pursued an MBA from Stanford University'. Forbes lists him as a Stanford drop-out and his own account says he left before finishing. We say he never finished.

Reliance says he has been on its board since 1977. His full-time role began after he came back from Stanford. Both dates are given. His own words place working 'almost full time' during his college years.
Mukesh said he was 'about 16 or 17' but mentioned it while describing his chemical engineering years, so the date is approximate. No agency or outcome is named, and we do not guess.

claim: When and how Dhirubhai worked in Aden
note: Mukesh (1998) dates the Shell job to 1954–57 and says it began at a petrol pump. A Reliance Group biography says he went in 1949 at 17 as a dispatch clerk at A. Besse & Co. Dhirubhai himself told Arab News's Farouk Luqman he was gas-station staff. We show all of these.

claim: When the family came back, and with how much
note: Mukesh (1998) and Reliance's history say 1957. Rediff (2015) and the Reliance Group biography say 1958. Mukesh and Rediff say about Rs 50,000. But in McKinsey (2025) Mukesh said his father came to Mumbai in 1960 with $100. We use the Rs 50,000 and 1957–58 account and record the other here.
Arab News (2012) mentions 'Majin' with Champaklal Damani; the Reliance Group biography says Reliance Commercial Corporation; Rediff (2015) another name. The text avoids naming it.

Anil Ambani (2002) described a one-bedroom flat for seven people. Some later profiles call it two-bedroom, and reports of the Simi Garewal interview recall more people. We follow Anil's first-hand description.

claim: How much time Dhirubhai spent with his children
note: Mukesh recalls Sundays reserved for family and yearly camping. Anil said he could not recall his father spending time with him during school or college. Both are shown as personal memories.

India's oil ministry and Oil & Gas Journal say 27 million tonnes a year in July 1999; Forbes (2006) says 600,000 barrels a day; The Hindu (2018) says 33 million tonnes; NS Energy says 18 million. An early draft used 18. We use 27, the official figure.
Reliance says 1.4 million barrels a day at a single location. NS Energy's older profile says 1.24 million. The oil ministry lists 33 plus 35.2 million tonnes a year. We use Reliance's figure.
Forbes says $3.4 billion for the refinery; Reuters called the complex a $6 billion project. The oil ministry dates commissioning to 14 July 1999, while Reliance's history page lists it under 2000.

Outlook gives annual output of 35.33, 20.88 and 9.77 mmscmd for 2011–14 against a planned 80. The field stopped in February 2020, but other fields in the same block began producing from December 2020, so 'the field' and 'the block' are not the same thing.

claim: Size of the KG-D6 government claim
note: Outlook India's December 2025 report of a claim above $30 billion rests on unnamed sources. It said an award was expected in 2026; we found none reported by 2 November 2026. This is separate from the $2.81 billion gas-migration dispute now before a Supreme Court-appointed mediator.

Outlook India says BP acquired 'its interest' in 2010 for $7.2 billion. BP's own 2011 announcement, reported by Oil & Gas Journal, shows the sum was for 30% of 23 blocks. We follow the 2011 announcement.

Offshore Technology (2019) wrote $75 billion for 20%. Argus (2020) says $75 billion was the value of the whole oil-to-chemicals business including debt, implying about $15 billion for 20%. We follow Argus.

Reuters counted 10 Lucknow stores closed; BBC said 30 ordered shut or held back including Varanasi; Business Today later said all 44 Fresh outlets in the state were shut. Job cuts were reported near 1,000. The Ranchi attack crowd was about 200 per PTI and 'thousands' per AFP.

claim: Share of Jio Platforms sold in 2020
note: Reports range from about 32.8% to 33%. We say 'about a third'.
The annual report and AGM speech give Rs 11,75,919 crore (gross). Some databases show about Rs 11.04 lakh crore, probably net of taxes. We use the company's figure.

Reports describe Reliance as declining to raise its bid in March 2010 rather than formally withdrawing it. We could not confirm a commonly quoted $15.5 billion plan valuation on a page we could open, so it was removed.

Size: about $3.1–3.2 billion, or Rs 30,213 crore. Subscription: 22.19 times (India TV). Demand: Rs 7.4 lakh crore (India TV) or over Rs 7.5 lakh crore (Akash Ambani). Time to fill: 100 minutes (India TV) or 95 (Akash Ambani). Applications: 1.39 crore (India TV) or over 1.3 crore (Akash Ambani). Market value: Rs 12.5 lakh crore or $131 billion at the open, about $137 billion at the close.

Forbes real-time: $88.8 billion, #22 (2 Nov 2026), up $8.5 billion in a day; $79.9 billion on 29 Oct. Bloomberg: $77.3 billion, #24 (1 Nov 2026). Reuters-based copy on 28 Oct called him Asia's richest per Forbes; VnExpress called him Asia's second-richest; Bloomberg called him third-richest. Forbes India's family list (read through a Billionaires.Africa summary) has him at $86.3 billion behind the Adani family at $112.7 billion.

claim: Supreme Court result in the Reliance Petroleum case (29 May 2026)
note: Fraud finding and Rs 447 crore order set aside, Rs 250 crore refunded, but the Rs 25 crore penalty for breaching disclosure rules stands. We read the factual and operative parts of the judgment, not all 135 pages closely, alongside The Hindu and The Economic Times. Reliance sold part of its stake: the judgment says 5% was planned, Mint says 4.1%.

claim: When Isha told him the home internet 'sucks'
note: Ambani said 2010 in 2016 and 2011 in his 2018 FT speech. The text gives both.

Times of India (2009) says he rose at 10:30 and worked noon to midnight; Open (2020) says he works late and starts before noon; a 2024 lifestyle piece says 5:30 am yoga without a first-hand source. We state the conflict and do not choose.

claim: His role in the 2019 Ericsson payment
note: Anil Ambani thanked him for support. ET Telecom's sources said about Rs 480 crore, an outright payment and not a loan. The company statement gave no details. BBC said he paid; PTI's headline says Rs 462 crore. The amount owed is reported as Rs 550 crore plus interest.
The Guardian said upwards of $600 million; BBC cited planners at $132–156 million; Al Jazeera called the numbers thinly sourced. The family has not disclosed a figure, so none is stated as fact.

Press reports put it at $1 billion or more (Crabtree calls that 'rumoured'). Bloomberg's index values it at about $410 million; we could not open Bloomberg's page directly to re-read that line. We give both.
The Times of London quoted him in May 2011. Tata Sons said the report was out of context and factually incorrect, and The Times stood by its story. Both are stated.
Nita Ambani (2024) and CNN call him strictly vegetarian. In an older Upper Crust interview he said he had always been vegetarian but ate eggs. The text shows both.

The Supreme Court (15 Sep 2025) accepted its team's finding of no violation and closed the complaints. The CITES Secretariat's later report, as reported by Mongabay, found no imports without permits but raised concerns about India's due diligence and recommended pausing some imports. Both are stated.
The Walton-style trust and family council are reports based on unnamed people (Bloomberg, Mint), never confirmed by Reliance, and are worded that way.

CREA says about 50% of Jamnagar's crude came from Russia in 2025. Reliance stopped Russian crude for its SEZ refinery from 20 November 2025 and said no Russian cargo was expected in January 2026. CREA noted three shipments later reported as bound for Jamnagar, so the position may have changed since.
